{{Quote|General Rahm Kota. He is attacking a critical Imperial shipyard above Nar Shaddaa. You will destroy him and bring me his lightsaber.|Darth Vader|<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>}}
This '''green-bladed lightsaber''' was the chosen weapon of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], and was a heavy-duty model that saw frequent use. During the Dark Times, the [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] wielded this lightsaber during his personal insurrection against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] dispatched [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]] to kill Kota and bring him the lightsaber. Starkiller blinded Kota with his own weapon, and though the Jedi escaped, Starkiller turned it over to Darth Vader.

Darth Vader later gave the lightsaber to Starkiller to replace [[Galen Marek's lightsaber|his original weapon]] after its loss. Masquerading as a Rebel, Starkiller wielded the lightsaber against various Imperial agents while assembling the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and modified it to suit his own needs. After Starkiller was betrayed by Darth Vader, he wielded the lightsaber against his former master and bested him. Starkiller perished in a subsequent confrontation with [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], and Vader destroyed the lightsaber.

==Specifications==
[[File:Kota_stormtrooper.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Rahm Kota executing a stormtrooper with his lightsaber]]

Kota's lightsaber was a heavy-duty model, with a solid hilt and an [[Blade emitter/Legends|emitter shroud]]. The hilt was covered with an interwoven fabric wrapping that acted as the grip of the lightsaber. Kota's lightsaber evidently saw frequent use, as by 2 BBY, the metal casing was heavily scratched and pitted. The blade originally featured a green crystal, and was perfectly serviceable. Uniquely, Kota kept his lightsaber in a custom [[Sheath/Legends|sheath]] on his back, rather than hanging from his belt as was the norm among Jedi.<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="TFUn" />

When [[Galen Marek]] took possession of the lightsaber, he found it to be perfectly adequate to his needs, but remained uncomfortable with the bold green blade. He was largely troubled by the issue of ownership, as he felt that it still belonged to Kota. He solved this by removing Kota's green crystal and replacing it with his [[Kento Marek|father's]] blue crystal, and concluded that this customization made the weapon ''his''. He noted that with this new crystal, the lightsaber handled more easily and possessed superior optical properties.<ref name="TFUn" />

==History==
{{Quote|Master Kota is dead?''"<br />"''Yes.''"<br />"''His lightsaber.|Darth Vader and Galen Marek as the latter presents Kota's lightsaber|<ref name="TFUn" />}}
[[File:Kota_vs_Starkiller.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Kota wielding his lightsaber against Galen Marek]]

Rahm Kota wielded this weapon frequently during his personal guerrilla war against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. When [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] dispatched [[Galen Marek]] to hunt down Kota, he ordered Marek to bring back Kota's lightsaber as proof of kill. In the ensuing duel aboard the [[TIE Fighter Construction Facility]] above [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], Marek won when he forced Kota's own blade into the Jedi's eyes, blinding him. Kota dropped his lightsaber before falling through a shattered viewport into Nar Shaddaa's upper atmosphere. Marek claimed the weapon before escaping himself.<ref name="TFUn" />

Returning to Darth Vader, Marek presented the weapon to his master. While Vader was pleased with his student's success, he felt that Marek was still unfocused and easily distracted, drawing the lightsaber on him to prove his point. The saber remained in Vader's possession until he dispatched Marek on a new mission. As [[Galen Marek's lightsaber|Marek's own Sith lightsaber]] had been lost in the vacuum when he was spaced, Vader provided him with Kota's lightsaber.<ref name="TFUn" />

[[File:MissiontoRaxusPrime.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Galen Marek wielding Kota's lightsaber with its new set of crystals]]

While Marek wielded the weapon effectively in combat, he had difficulty using it in his meditations, his favorite exercise being to stare into his lightsaber blade to focus his fury. He overcame this when he replaced Kota's green crystal with [[Kento Marek|his father's]] blue crystal, retrieved on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. He found that the weapon performed better with this new crystal, though he noted that the aqua hue made him think more of oceans and rain than the blood and fire fostered by his original, [[Synthetic lightsaber crystal/Legends|red]] lightsaber. The blue blade saw first use during his [[second mission to Raxus Prime]].<ref name="TFUn" />

When Galen Marek was ultimately betrayed by Darth Vader, he rejected the Sith and fought back. [[Battle on Death Star I|Assaulting]] the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] in a bid to rescue the captured leaders of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], Marek wielded the lightsaber against various divisions of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]. Ultimately, the weapon saw use against Darth Vader, and Marek proved himself the superior duelist, bashing off the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord's]] [[Darth Vader's armor#Functionality|helmet]]. Galen Marek even attacked [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], using the lightsaber to absorb his [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] attacks while countering with telekinesis to save his Jedi mentor and the other leaders of the Rebel Alliance from the anger of Palpatine and stormtrooper reinforcements.<ref name="TFUvg" />

Galen Marek ultimately perished in the engagement, the lightsaber found with his corpse. Darth Vader destroyed the weapon, crushing it beneath his [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetic heel]].<ref name="TFUn" />

===Backups/replacement===
[[File:Kota_arrests_Vader.png|thumb|right|250px|Kota holding Darth Vader at bladepoint with one of his replacement lightsabers]]

General Kota's loss of the weapon did not prove debilitating for him, as he quickly gained a replacement. While hiding out on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]], he carried a blue lightsaber, wielding it during [[Skirmish on Cloud City|his escape]]. He took up a new green blade, possibly the same lightsaber with new crystals, during the [[Corellian Treaty]], unsuccessfully wielding it against Darth Vader. This weapon was cosmetically identical to his original lightsaber, and it, or a similar replacement, likely saw continued use during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TFUvg" /><ref name="TFU2vg">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

General Kota wielded his weapon during his tenure in the [[Tarko-se Arena]], slaying numerous beasts and [[Gladiator/Legends|Gladiators]] with it. He also used it during the [[Battle near the Itani Nebula]] and the [[Assault on Kamino]]. At the conclusion of the latter, General Kota held a captured Darth Vader at bladepoint with the lightsaber while the Sith Lord was detained.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

==Behind the scenes==
The loss of Galen Marek's lightsaber, and his subsequent use of Kota's lightsaber, is a plot element exclusive to the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|novelization]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', with the various game versions and the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (graphic novel)|graphic novel adaptation]] depicting Marek continuing to use his original lightsaber, albeit with a blue blade. However, in the inconsistencies between the various game versions of the story on numerous plot points, the novelization is generally accepted as the final word, so the replacement of Marek's lightsaber with Kota's is considered part of the [[Star Wars Legends|official storyline]].<ref name="TFUvg" />

The fabric wrapping around the handle of Kota's lightsaber makes it resemble the grip of a traditional Japanese sword, such as a katana. This is presumably to bring it in line with Kota's general design theme of a ronin, or wandering samurai.
